newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call money unchanged, term rates lower.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call money unchanged, term rates lower.

text.p: Philippine call money was unchanged at 16.03125 percent despite the usual weekend covering which built up Monday turnover, traders said.
They attributed it to excess liquidity in the market, and the decision of the Central Bank to keep its overnight borrowing rate at 16.0 percent.
Turnover rose to 16.789 billion pesos with done rates ranging from 16.03125 percent to 16.25 percent.
The highly-liquid market situation pushed down the indicative secondary quotes for Treasury bills.

"Some banks lowered their offer rates to discourage buyers. They still believe that the rates will go down further, so they want to keep previous week's bills which offer relatively higher rates," one trader said.
Traders were predicting the benchmark 91-day T-bill rate to slide near 11.60 percent, which is the rate being offered by the Central Bank for its special series 86-day bills.
"We still see rates to go down by 20 to 30 basis points this afternoon," one trader said. The bellwether rate was at 120.892 percent in last Monday's auction.
A survey of eight commercial banks showed that offered rates for the three-month bills ranged from 10.5 to 10.8 percent, while bid rates were at 10.625 to 10.90 percent.
